thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: regional-health-controller detected repeated health-check flips across regions for route /api/v1/generate (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Creating incident INC-2025-0423 and paging oncall.
pagerbot: Paging @sre-oncall-maria (oncall for SRE rotation) — Pager: SEV2 — >15% errors to customers, spike in latency, region failovers detected. Links: https://redwood-infra/ops/incidents/INC-2025-0423
sre-oncall-maria: ack here, looking. grabbing logs + topology. anyone already in triage? :eyes:
ryan.k: I saw the alert via tracing — looks like health-check responses from model-serving nodes are 200 but probe health aggregated as fail because of variant mismatch. Will pull more data now.
lee.s: Noted customer impact in Support: CS reports 12 distinct customers seeing degraded responses or timeouts in last 30m. Ticket examples: #CS-9981, #CS-9983. Prod dashboard: error rate 18% and request routing churn high.
jordan.t: From routing telemetry, requests are bouncing between us-east and us-west every ~45s. EU picks up overflow then drops back. We're seeing a sawtooth in active connections per region.
sre-oncall-maria: Can you paste the failing probe logs? also which probe type — liveness or full-model-query?
ryan.k: Pasting snippet:
```
2025-04-23T14:02:12Z probe-service us-east instance-x healthchk: variant="q5_8bit" kernel_sig=0x1a2b - ok
2025-04-23T14:02:12Z probe-service us-west instance-y healthchk: variant="q4_8bit" kernel_sig=0x1a3c - mismatch -> mark unhealthy
2025-04-23T14:02:57Z router region-fallback: route /api/v1/generate -> failover(us-west->us-east)
2025-04-23T14:03:30Z probe-service eu instance-z healthchk: variant="q5_8bit" kernel_sig=0x1a2b - ok
2025-04-23T14:04:00Z router region-fallback: route /api/v1/generate -> failover(eu->us-east)
```
ryan.k: Looks like health-check compares kernel signature + model variant. us-west nodes are reporting a different quantized build (q4_8bit) than the routing expects (q5_8bit), so router flips that region out. Then autoscaler/probe reconciliation brings nodes back and it flips again.
eng-platform: Is there a rollout in us-west currently? I see a partial canary from earlier this morning for 034-quant-opt.
lee.s: AWS tags show a deployment window at 13:50 UTC to us-west pool: image: rwinf/model-server:034-quant-opt. Could be related.
sre-oncall-maria: Temporarily disabling health-check variant-strictness for route /api/v1/generate to stop cascading failovers. Applying policy: health-check.match_strict = false for 10m. If we do that we accept potential quality mismatch but keep availability. Thoughts?
ryan.k: +1 from runtime team. We should also pin routing policy to prefer home region and disable automatic multi-region fallback for this route until we confirm variant compatibility.
jordan.t: Making that change now: `kubectl patch configmap routing-policy -n redwood --patch '{"data":{"/api/v1/generate":"prefer-local,disable-cross-region-fallback"}}'` — applied. Router config reload started.
sre-oncall-maria: Confirming health-check relax applied: `PATCH /internal/probe/config` -> success. Now observing request churn falling.
incidents-bot: [INC-2025-0423] Status update: mitigation in-progress, change set applied by jordan.t, probe strictness relaxed by sre-oncall-maria. Impact: partial — errors down from 18% to 6%. ETA for rollback to default: next steps.
cs-ops: Customer notice drafted, pinging impacted accounts with temporary degraded perf note. Holding for 30m to ensure stability before broad notification.
lee.s: Telemetry: after change, us-west healthy and steady. However logs show model-quality regression in ~2% of responses when falling back to q4_8bit (some tokenization artifacts). No obvious semantic regressions for the majority.
ryan.k: Root cause summary so far: a partial canary published a q4 quantized variant to us-west but routing health-checks require exact variant match; when router sees mismatch it flips region and traffic oscillates. Two contributing issues: 1) rollout gating didn't update routing compatibility metadata, 2) health-check strictness is too brittle for small quant differences.
eng-platform: Proposed short-term fixes: a) fix rollout tool to populate variant compatibility in the model-catalog metadata; b) change health-check to accept canonical equivalence (kernel_sig family matching) for 1 hour; c) add 5s debounce to region-fallback circuit.
sre-oncall-maria: Agreed. For now we'll keep strictness relaxed and keep disable-cross-region-fallback on /api/v1/generate for 1 hour. I'll monitor for customer escalations.
jordan.t: Rolling back the canary in us-west (to previous image 033-stable) as a fast mitigation. Triggering deployment rollback: `deployctl rollback --pool us-west --image rwinf/model-server:033-stable --grace 30s`
incidents-bot: rollback job queued (job-8421). Notifying eng-runtime.
ryan.k: Observing rollback start. If rollback finishes and metrics stabilize we can re-enable strict health-checks and cross-region fallback with a compatibility flag.
lee.s: CS reports initial customer replies: some appreciative, one large customer (ACME Corp) still seeing transient errors during the ~30m window. CS will escalate if we see further traffic.
cs-ops: ACME contact pinged. No open SLA breach yet, but we'll prepare a follow-up summary and potential credit if their job was affected.
sre-oncall-maria: Rollback finished. Telemetry shows stable routing, errors back to baseline ~1.3%. Re-enabling cross-region fallback would risk re-triggering; hold for postmortem. I'll start incident timeline and assign postmortem owners.
eng-platform: Creating follow-up tickets:
- PLAT-2456: rollout tool to attach model-variant metadata -> owner: ryan.k
- PLAT-2457: health-check equivalence rule and debounce logic -> owner: lee.s
- PLAT-2458: routing-policy guardrails for canaries -> owner: jordan.t
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2025-0423 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to SEV3. Assigning postmortem to eng-platform.
sre-oncall-maria: Handing off to night oncall @sre-night (cc eng-platform). If symptoms recur escalate to oncall. Postmortem draft due EOD tomorrow. Good job team :clap:
ryan.k: quick note: include perf vs quality metrics for q4_8bit vs q5_8bit in the postmortem — runtime perf wins may have driven the canary decision.
cs-ops: we'll log customer impact and timeline in the postmortem. Let us know if we should proactively offer credits to impacted customers.
eng-platform: Thanks all. Follow-ups created and owners assigned. I'll add telemetry dashboards for variant mismatch alerts to catch this earlier.
sre-oncall-maria: closing this thread for now, will update postmortem link when ready. If anyone sees new flapping reopen thread or ping me directly. :heavy_check_mark:
